chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever is killed due to his injustice (or for his cause), he is a martyr.'

key_terms.مَظْلِمَتِهِ: His injustice / his cause (referring to the person being wronged or fighting for their rights)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a person to be considered a martyr (shahid) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this concise yet profound statement from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), linking the status of martyrdom directly to the cause of death rather than merely the manner of fighting. This hadith expands the traditional understanding of *shahid* to include those killed due to personal injustice or for defending their rights, emphasizing that dying while upholding justice or enduring oppression grants the same spiritual merit as those who fall in battle. It serves as a key textual basis in Shia jurisprudence for determining the legal and spiritual status of martyrs in various contexts of conflict and persecution.
